recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12699; any future consent category terminology change should be handled through THO/UTG.
issue_request: FHIR-12699 was Published / Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2/STU3 Consent quality warnings: add a Consent.category example, reorder Consent elements to match W5, rename the reserved search parameter named security, define the old cat1 consent category code, and rename the duplicate ConsentStatus value set.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 612068c15886b6624c44de5d656417bcfa7d76d3, whose subject explicitly includes GF#12699. That commit added a category-bearing Consent example, added the cat1 definition, moved Consent spreadsheet rows/order, and changed the old search parameter from security to securitylabel.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini. The current R6 resource model has changed since STU3, but status/category remain early in the resource, Consent.category is used in examples, the value set is now Consent State, core no longer owns the consent category CodeSystem after UTG/THO migration, and current THO supplies defined consent category codes. FHIR-17154 later renamed securitylabel to security-label according to FHIR search parameter naming conventions.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reintroducing the old securityLabel/securitylabel spelling or old cat1 core CodeSystem content would conflict with later source history and the current source-of-truth split between FHIR core and THO.

related_jiras.note: Published later Consent issue renamed securitylabel to security-label, explaining why the current source intentionally differs from the 2017 FHIR-12699 spelling.
